blogs.title: The Telomere Masquerader: Recognizing Adult-Onset TBD Without the Dyskeratosis Triad
blogs.description: Young adults with pancytopenia, premature greying, hepatosplenomegaly, osteoporosis, neuropathy, or unexplained organ fibrosis can harbor a telomere biology disorder (TBD) even without the classic mucocutaneous triad of dyskeratosis congenita. This post outlines red flags, a pragmatic diagnostic pathway (when to order flow-FISH telomere length testing and when to escalate to exome panels), and common pitfalls that delay diagnosis by anchoring on nutritional or autoimmune explanations.

blogs.title: When B12 Deficiency Isn’t the Whole Story: Untangling Ineffective Erythropoiesis, DAT Positivity, and Telomere Risk
blogs.description: Severe B12 deficiency can dominate the hematology picture with dimorphism, hypersegmented neutrophils, and marrow erythroid hyperplasia—yet a low reticulocyte count and disproportionate cytopenias should prompt a search for coexisting marrow vulnerability such as a TBD. We dissect how to interpret a positive DAT in this context, differentiate immune destruction from intramedullary hemolysis/ineffective erythropoiesis, and avoid premature immunosuppression while correcting deficiencies and planning surveillance for evolving marrow failure.

blogs.title: PARN on the Edge: How to Manage a VUS When the Phenotype Fits
blogs.description: Monoallelic PARN variants often track with pulmonary fibrosis and/or bone marrow failure, but many are reported as variants of uncertain significance (VUS). Using this case, we walk through real-world variant adjudication: domain-level evidence (R3H), gene constraint, ACMG criteria (PM1/PM2/PP2/PP3), the role of age-adjusted flow-FISH to support pathogenicity, strategies for periodic reclassification (ClinVar, functional data, segregation), and how to counsel and manage patients when the genetics are suggestive but not definitive.

blogs.title: Two Fibroses, One Biology: Hepatic and Pulmonary Fibrosis in Telomere Syndromes
blogs.description: Hepatic fibrosis is under-recognized in TBDs, while pulmonary fibrosis is a well-known driver of morbidity. We review evidence for liver involvement across telomere disorders, propose a screening bundle (LFTs, ultrasound, elastography, variceal assessment when indicated) alongside lung surveillance (HRCT, PFTs), discuss antifibrotic use in short telomere cohorts, and highlight medication and exposure precautions that matter when both organs are at risk.

blogs.title: Transplanting on Short Telomeres: Conditioning Choices, Antifibrotics, and Immunosuppression Pitfalls
blogs.description: TBDs change the risk calculus for hematopoietic and solid-organ transplantation: cytopenias, hepatic toxicity, and poor wound healing are more likely. We outline HSCT indications and reduced-intensity, radiation-sparing conditioning principles; precautions with myelosuppressive agents (for example, azathioprine, high-dose alkylators); peri-transplant infectious risk and CMV vigilance; the role of androgens (danazol/nandrolone) as a bridge; and practical considerations for lung transplantation in short telomere patients.

blogs.title: After the Diagnosis: Building a Practical Surveillance and Family Plan for Telomere Biology Disorders
blogs.description: Turn a TBD label into action: set up organ-specific monitoring (CBC with retic, HRCT/PFT intervals, liver elastography/ultrasound, bone density), malignancy surveillance (marrow failure progression, oral/skin exams), vaccination and infection-prevention guidance, and lifestyle counseling (smoking/alcohol avoidance, marrow-sparing drug lists). We also cover cascade testing and the nuances of using telomere length versus genetics in relatives, reproductive counseling, and triggers for early referral to transplant centers.
